questions.q: What made the mp3 format technologically appealing?
a: It compressed audio to sound indistinguishable from a CD
It stored songs at a higher quality than any CD
It allowed music to play on more devices than mp2
It made albums cheaper to manufacture than before
questions.why: Lesson 1 says German scientists worked for years to compress audio while keeping CD-quality sound.

questions.q: Where was the mp3 format developed?
a: At the Fraunhofer Institute in Germany
At a record label's research lab in Japan
At an American university funded by Phillips
At the MPEG headquarters in Switzerland
questions.why: Lesson 1 says scientists at the German Fraunhofer Institute began developing the format in 1987.

questions.q: What did Fraunhofer do in 1995 that helped spark music piracy?
a: It gave away its mp3 conversion software for free
It sold mp3 players at a steep discount
It published instructions for copying CDs
It licensed the format only to small labels
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Fraunhofer released WinPlay3 for free, which helped users rip and share songs.

questions.q: Why did the mp3 win its format war against the CD?
a: The internet let people rip and share files easily
Record labels refused to release music on CD
CD players became too expensive to manufacture
The MPEG organization banned the CD format
questions.why: Lesson 2 says broadband and easy file sharing made mp3 the preferred format and made piracy commonplace.

questions.q: What does the summary say is now threatening the mp3?
a: Streaming services are replacing downloaded files
Vinyl records are outselling digital music
Governments are banning compressed audio formats
Artists are refusing to release music online
questions.why: Lesson 3 says streaming has pushed the mp3 toward retirement as listeners stop buying and owning files.
